title: Win32 process lifecycle, reverse-order unwind, and real-Windows Job acceptance
description:
SPIDR child 2b of 2, split from task-a02496064e9e4e87a888cc112830d7a4 by architect-5aba94da on plan shape. Human confirmed the split in the REPL before it was created. See sibling task-885a46e9fb274a94b12faa826ba580dc (child 2a) for the measured evidence behind the split.

DEPENDS ON task-885a46e9fb274a94b12faa826ba580dc (child 2a: Cargo.toml Win32_System_Threading feature, the win32.rs split, construction-side NativeOp variants, the process-side call-table trait, src/system_process.rs, src/process.rs, tests/process_sweep.rs). Do not start until 2a is DONE, and RE-MEASURE its landed symbols before planning rather than trusting this description -- 2a's own planning was forced to correct two stale claims inherited from its parent, and this description is subject to exactly the same decay. This task ADDS lifecycle arms to modules 2a creates; it must not re-create the crate, the call table, the handle type, any Job operation from child 1, or any construction step from 2a.

Objective: tear down what 2a built, correctly and in reverse order, and prove the whole primitive on a real Windows kernel rather than only through the injected call table.

Deliverable, inside packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/:
- src/win32.rs: add the lifecycle-side NativeOp variants and extend NativeOp::ALL and its array length; add the lifecycle arms to the process-side call-table trait 2a declared. Must still land <=250 lines -- if 2a left it near the bar, split by responsibility rather than by reformatting.
- src/system_process.rs: add the real windows-sys impls for the lifecycle arms (WaitForSingleObject, GetExitCodeProcess, TerminateProcess). GetProcessTimes and QueryFullProcessImageNameW may already be present from 2a's identity work -- check before adding. Must still land <=250 lines; split it if 2a left it near the bar.
- src/lifecycle.rs (NEW): wait, exit query, terminate, ActiveProcesses==0 query, and the full reverse-order unwind of partial construction.
- src/lib.rs: module declaration and re-exports.
- tests/process_sweep.rs: extend 2a's sweep to cover every lifecycle arm without weakening any assertion 2a landed.
- tests/real_windows.rs (NEW): focused real-Windows acceptance.

The unwind protocol has two distinct regimes and the boundary between them is the membership proof, not the CreateProcessW call. A PRE-membership fault means a child exists that the Job may not contain, so it must be terminated and awaited DIRECTLY. A POST-membership fault means the Job owns the child, so terminating the Job and waiting for ActiveProcesses==0 is the correct and sufficient action. Collapsing these two into one path is the defect this task exists to prevent.

Supported floor is Windows 10 / Server 2016. This host is win32 x64, so the real-Windows acceptance tests are honestly runnable here and must actually be run -- not marked #[ignore] and not stubbed.

NOT IN SCOPE: Node/stdio framing, JavaScript hostile-input validation, Claude discovery/grants, daemon/store authority, receipts, or any public @moe/runner export.

Production consumer: task-af3d7bc8af2146cf92d98557ed0e90c0 (Windows Job broker protocol), then task-4d1f8ba54cb6476c930c46b413f882aa.

Verification: cargo test --locked --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-core && cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-core
definitionOfDone: src/lifecycle.rs performs wait, exit query, terminate and the ActiveProcesses==0 query using the ORIGINAL Job, process and thread handles retained from construction, and never reopens a process by PID. A test proves the retained-handle path by asserting no open-by-PID arm exists in the call table at all -- absence of the capability, not merely absence of its use.

The API returns PID plus creation-time and final-image identity, and reports no started, exited or tree-dead outcome before the matching membership, identity, exit or ActiveProcesses==0 fact has been queried successfully. Proved by failing each query arm in turn and asserting the specific NativeOp reported -- never merely that the call refused.

Reverse-order unwind is proved for BOTH regimes separately: a PRE-membership fault terminates the child and awaits it directly, and a POST-membership fault terminates the Job and waits for ActiveProcesses==0. Two distinct call-log assertions, one per regime; a single shared path that happens to satisfy both is a failure of this item.

A cleanup whose outcome is unknown is retained as uncertain and never converted to success: a failing terminate, wait or close during unwind surfaces as an error carrying its own NativeOp, while the FIRST error that caused the unwind is the one returned to the caller.

tests/process_sweep.rs covers every lifecycle arm with the exact NativeOp and a distinct Win32 error code per arm, asserts a nonzero exact case count, and cross-checks the produced op set against the production NativeOp enum so an unreached arm fails the suite. Every assertion 2a landed still passes unweakened, verified by mutating one production arm and confirming the suite goes red.

tests/real_windows.rs runs (not #[ignore], not stubbed) and proves on a real kernel that a suspended marker process cannot execute before the membership and assignment proof, and that terminating the configured Job leaves ActiveProcesses==0. It launches a direct executable plus argv and never uses taskkill, a command shell, or PID-enumeration-only cleanup. Any marker file or temp path it creates is removed on every exit path, including failure.

Every Rust production source is <=250 physical lines measured by `grep -c '' <file>` with per-file counts recorded; child 1's and 2a's crate, call table, handle type, Job operations and process construction are reused unchanged; and the locked test and release-build commands both exit 0 with no committed target, executable, debug or probe artifact.
taskRails: The unwind boundary is the MEMBERSHIP PROOF, not the CreateProcessW call. Pre-membership faults terminate and await the child directly; post-membership faults terminate the Job and wait for ActiveProcesses==0. These are two paths and must be tested as two paths.
Native failures carry a closed operation enum and numeric Win32 error only; never echo executable, argv, cwd, environment, or raw handle values.
Keep every Rust production source focused, target and hard-cap <=250 physical lines; split before 400. Never commit Cargo target output, binaries, marker files or probe artifacts.

This is a native primitive, not authority: no @moe/runner root export, Claude policy, activation grant, daemon/store call, or evidence claim. ActiveProcesses==0 is an observation about a live handle, not proof of tree death.

Reuse child 1's crate, call-table trait, RAII handle and Job operations, and 2a's process construction, unchanged. Do not recreate, fork, or reimplement them, and do not reimplement any production authority inside tests/real_windows.rs.
Real-Windows tests must actually run on this win32 host. Marking them #[ignore], gating them off, or stubbing the kernel interaction fails this task outright.

implementationPlan.description: HARD GATE: RE-MEASURE 2a's SEAM BEFORE WRITING ANYTHING. This plan was written while 2a was in flight and uncommitted, so every symbol below is provisional. Write nothing in this step. Confirm ALL of the following, and if any one differs, STOP and call moe.report_blocked with the difference rather than adapting silently: (a) 2a is committed -- `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD -- packages/runner/src/platform/windows` lists src/process.rs, src/win32/process_calls.rs, src/win32/system_job.rs, src/win32/system_process.rs and tests/process_sweep.rs, and `git status --porcelain` over the crate is clean. If 2a is still uncommitted, stop here regardless of anything else -- four of this task's eight owned files are ones 2a is actively editing. (b) `NativeOp::ALL` is declared `[NativeOp; 15]`. (c) `ProcessCalls` still has `type AttributeList` and the ten methods named in planningNotes, with `is_process_in_job -> Result<bool, _>` and `resume_thread -> Result<u32, _>`. (d) `ContainedProcess` still takes `job: &Job<'c, C>` in `create` and does not retain it. (e) `Job::handle()` is still pub(crate). Then record `grep -c ''` for every Rust source, run the task's exact verification command as the PRE-DIFF baseline required by the path-attributed-baseline rail, and record `git rev-parse HEAD` and the merge-base.

EXTEND THE VOCABULARY AND THE SEAM. In src/win32.rs add exactly four NativeOp variants -- WaitForProcess, QueryExitCode, TerminateProcess, QueryImageName -- and extend NativeOp::ALL to `[NativeOp; 19]` in declaration order. Do NOT add variants for job termination or accounting: child 1's TerminateJob and QueryAccounting already exist and the post-membership unwind regime reuses them. In src/win32/process_calls.rs add the matching arms to the EXISTING `ProcessCalls` trait rather than declaring a new trait -- `ContainedProcess` is already bounded on `Win32Calls + ProcessCalls`, so a third trait would force a signature change across 2a's type and every double. The arms are: `wait_for_process(process, timeout_ms) -> Result<WaitOutcome, NativeError>`, `exit_code(process) -> Result<u32, NativeError>`, `terminate_process(process) -> Result<(), NativeError>`, `image_name(process) -> Result<Vec<u16>, NativeError>`. Define `WaitOutcome` as a closed enum with Signalled / TimedOut / Abandoned -- WAIT_TIMEOUT and WAIT_ABANDONED are legitimate Ok values, NOT errors, and only WAIT_FAILED becomes Err. Document at the seam that WaitForSingleObject returns WAIT_EVENT and not a BOOL, so `!= WAIT_OBJECT_0 -> Err` is wrong. Keep both files <=250 lines.

TDD RED, AND PIN THE STILL_ACTIVE TRAP FIRST. Extend the scripted double in tests/process_sweep.rs with the four new arms, a programmable WaitOutcome, and a programmable exit code, WITHOUT weakening any assertion 2a landed. Then write the failing tests for the exit-query discipline before any production code exists: (a) an exit query made with no prior successful wait yields the UNKNOWN case, asserted by its reason code, NEVER a numeric exit code; (b) an exit query after a wait that returned TimedOut likewise yields UNKNOWN; (c) only after a wait returning Signalled does the query yield Exited(code); (d) a process whose real exit code IS 259 is reported as Exited(259) after a confirmed Signalled wait -- proving the design distinguishes it from STILL_ACTIVE rather than blacklisting the value. Case (d) is the one that catches a lazy `if code == 259 { unknown }` implementation, so it is not optional. Also write the four-outcome wait tests: Signalled, TimedOut and Abandoned are Ok values; only WAIT_FAILED is Err carrying NativeOp::WaitForProcess and the real code.

GREEN, PART 1: THE QUERY SURFACE. Create src/lifecycle.rs with the wait, exit-query, terminate and ActiveProcesses==0 operations, generic over `C: Win32Calls + ProcessCalls`, taking the retained handles and `&Job` rather than ever reopening by PID. Model the exit result as a closed enum whose Exited(code) variant is UNCONSTRUCTIBLE without a wait that returned Signalled -- make that a type-level property, not a runtime check a caller can skip, because GetExitCodeProcess returns STILL_ACTIVE (259) both for a running process and for one that genuinely exited with 259, and those are indistinguishable from the call alone. Anything else stays UNKNOWN, per epic rail 4. Add the final-image identity query (QueryFullProcessImageNameW with PROCESS_NAME_WIN32) and expose PID and creation time by delegating to 2a's ContainedProcess accessors rather than re-querying. Nothing here reports started, exited or tree-dead before the corresponding fact has been queried successfully. This step makes step 3's tests pass.

GREEN, PART 2: THE TWO-REGIME UNWIND, wired into construction. Add the unwind protocol to src/lifecycle.rs and invoke it from `ContainedProcess::create` in src/process.rs, which is the only place a partial-construction fault can be observed. THE BOUNDARY IS THE MEMBERSHIP PROOF, NOT CreateProcessW. Before membership is proven, a child exists that the Job may not contain, so unwind must terminate THAT PROCESS by its handle and wait for it directly. After membership is proven the Job owns the child, so unwind terminates the JOB (child 1's terminate_job) and waits for ActiveProcesses==0 (child 1's query_active_processes) -- and it must WAIT for the count to reach zero rather than sampling once, because TerminateJobObject returns before the processes are gone. These are two paths and must remain two; a single shared path that happens to satisfy both fails DoD item 3. Cleanup outcomes are retained as uncertain and never laundered: a terminate, wait or close that fails during unwind surfaces as an error carrying its own NativeOp, while the FIRST error -- the one that caused the unwind -- is what the caller receives. Follow the ordering child 1 established in handle.rs: attempt every cleanup even after one fails, so nothing leaks, and let the first error win. If lifecycle.rs would exceed 250 lines, split the unwind into src/unwind.rs; that contingency is pre-authorised and stays inside the file ceiling.

REAL WIN32 IMPL. Add the four lifecycle arms to src/win32/system_process.rs, the file 2a created, keeping every unsafe block behind a SAFETY comment in the established style. Check first whether 2a already implemented creation_time via GetProcessTimes and whether image_name is present -- add only what is missing rather than duplicating. Specifics: WaitForSingleObject returns WAIT_EVENT, so map WAIT_OBJECT_0 to Signalled, WAIT_TIMEOUT to TimedOut, WAIT_ABANDONED to Abandoned, and ONLY WAIT_FAILED to Err with GetLastError -- a BOOL-style check here is a bug. GetExitCodeProcess and TerminateProcess are ordinary BOOL checks. QueryFullProcessImageNameW takes PROCESS_NAME_WIN32 and an in/out size in WCHARs, not bytes, and updates that size on success, so the returned buffer must be truncated to the reported length rather than to its capacity. Reuse the existing last_error and check helpers instead of writing new ones. If the file would exceed 250 lines, split the lifecycle arms into src/win32/system_lifecycle.rs -- pre-authorised, still inside the ceiling.

COMPLETE THE SWEEP, INCLUDING BOTH UNWIND REGIMES. Extend tests/process_sweep.rs to cover every lifecycle arm: one frozen Case per failable arm with a DISTINCT Win32 error code, an `assert_eq!` on the case count so a sweep that generates zero cases cannot pass, and the exact NativeOp plus exact code asserted per case. Update the totality cross-check to the new vocabulary -- the produced process-op set equals a hand-written PROCESS_OPS list exactly, every member is in NativeOp::ALL, and PROCESS_OPS.len() + 6 == NativeOp::ALL.len() == 19. That count assertion is also what proves DoD item 1's absence of an open-by-PID arm: adding one would require a variant and would break the count. Add the TWO REGIME TESTS as separate call-log assertions: a fault injected BEFORE the membership proof must produce a log containing terminate-process then wait-for-process and NOT terminate-job; a fault injected AFTER the membership proof must produce terminate-job then a repeated active-process query reaching zero, and NOT terminate-process. Assert the whole recorded vector in each, not a containment. Add the uncertain-cleanup test: a terminate that fails during unwind surfaces its own NativeOp while the caller still receives the original first error. Confirm every assertion 2a landed still passes unweakened.

REAL WINDOWS ACCEPTANCE. Create tests/real_windows.rs. These run for real on this win32 host -- no #[ignore], no cfg gate, no stub; that is task rail 6 and marking them skipped fails the task outright. Resolve the executable from %SystemRoot%\\System32\\PING.EXE rather than hardcoding C:\\Windows, pass argv directly, and never invoke a command shell, taskkill, or PID enumeration. Build the three required inherited handles by opening the NUL device three times as inheritable via CreateFileW; that is test fixture setup, not production authority. TEST A, a suspended process cannot execute before the proofs: create `ping -n 1 127.0.0.1` suspended inside a configured Job; BEFORE resume assert IsProcessInJob is already true and ActiveProcesses==1, and assert a bounded wait (roughly 500ms) returns TimedOut even though this command would exit in well under a second unresumed -- that timeout IS the observation that the thread never ran; then resume and assert the wait returns Signalled and the exit code becomes readable only after it. TEST B, terminating the Job leaves nothing: create `ping -n 60 127.0.0.1` in the Job, assert ActiveProcesses==1, terminate the Job, wait on the retained process handle until Signalled, then assert ActiveProcesses==0 -- wait for it, never sleep-and-sample. Close every handle on every path including panic, and treat KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE as a backstop rather than the primary cleanup.

WIRE UP AND AUDIT SIZE. In src/lib.rs add `mod lifecycle;` (and `mod unwind;` if step 5 split it) and re-export the new public surface -- the lifecycle operations, the wait-outcome enum and the exit-result enum -- keeping every item on exactly one public path as the existing comment requires. Update the crate and module docs that still describe lifecycle and unwind as belonging to a future sibling task: src/process.rs and src/job.rs both carry scope comments naming task-af99cf14 as out-of-scope future work, and those are now false. Correct them rather than leaving a comment that contradicts the code. Then audit every Rust production source with `grep -c '' <file>` and record each count: lib.rs, win32.rs, win32/process_calls.rs, win32/system_job.rs, win32/system_process.rs, lifecycle.rs, process.rs, job.rs, handle.rs, plus any file created by a pre-authorised split. Every one must be <=250. Split by responsibility, never by reformatting, and do not proceed with a file over the bar.

VERIFY, ATTACK, COMMIT. (a) Run the task's exact verification command -- the locked test run AND the locked release build -- and paste the real output; both must exit 0, and real_windows.rs must appear in the results as RUN, not filtered or ignored. State the test counts. (b) Compare against the step-1 baseline: any repo-wide red must be shown to exist at the merge-base too, or it is yours. (c) MUTATION DRILL, required by epic rail 6 because none of these defects are visible in a green suite: make the exit query return the raw code without requiring a prior Signalled wait and confirm the STILL_ACTIVE tests go RED; swap the two unwind regimes so a pre-membership fault terminates the Job and confirm the regime tests go RED; make WAIT_TIMEOUT return Err and confirm both the four-outcome test and real_windows TEST A go RED; delete one entry from PROCESS_OPS and confirm the totality assertion goes RED. Restore each and re-confirm green, then verify by reading the file contents -- not by trusting a clean git status -- that no mutation survived, because a foreign whole-tree commit can capture a drill edit. (d) Adversarial pass: NativeError still exposes only op and code; RawHandle still has no Debug; no executable path, argv, cwd, environment or handle value reaches an error, a log, or a panic message. (e) Confirm no target output, executable, marker or probe artifact is staged. (f) `git status --porcelain`, unstage anything foreign with `git restore --staged`, commit by explicit pathspec over this task's owned paths only, and verify with `git show --stat`.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
WHERE THE LIFECYCLE ARMS GO. Chose extending the existing `ProcessCalls` trait in src/win32/process_calls.rs (110 -> ~160 lines, under the bar). Rejected a separate `LifecycleCalls` trait: `ContainedProcess<'c, C: Win32Calls + ProcessCalls>` already carries that exact bound, so a third trait would force a signature change on 2a's type and every impl and test double -- churn in a sibling's file for no isolation benefit.

HOW THE UNWIND REACHES THE JOB. `ContainedProcess` does not retain the Job and this plan does NOT add it. Inside `ContainedProcess::create` the Job is already a parameter and in scope, which is the only place partial-construction unwind can run. For post-construction lifecycle calls the caller passes `&Job` explicitly. DoD item 1 is satisfied either way -- the point is that the ORIGINAL handle is used rather than reopening by PID, and a `&Job` the caller already holds is the original handle.

REAL-WINDOWS PROOF WITHOUT A MARKER FILE OR A HELPER BINARY. Rejected `src/bin/marker.rs` even though Cargo autobins would discover it without a manifest edit: epic rail 5 forbids probe files in commits and a marker helper reads as exactly that, and it would push the file count to 10. Rejected a filesystem marker copied by robocopy/xcopy: a temp path plus cleanup-on-every-path obligation, for a weaker signal. CHOSE a wait-based proof using PING.EXE resolved from %SystemRoot%: before resume, a bounded wait on the process handle returns WAIT_TIMEOUT even though `ping -n 1` would exit in well under a second, which IS the observation that the thread never ran; after resume the same wait returns WAIT_OBJECT_0. No filesystem, no race, no cleanup obligation, no shell, and it exercises the very arms this task adds. `ping -n 60` gives the long-lived process for the terminate test.

INHERITED HANDLES IN THE ACCEPTANCE TEST. ProcessSpec demands exactly three. Open the NUL device three times as inheritable via CreateFileW in test setup. That is test FIXTURE code, not production authority, so it does not violate the rail against reimplementing authority in real_windows.rs -- and it keeps the child's output off the test console.

PROVING ABSENCE OF AN OPEN-BY-PID ARM (DoD item 1). There is no way to assert a method does not exist, so the proof is the closed vocabulary: `NativeOp::ALL` is a fixed-size array whose length is part of its type, and the sweeps assert the exact total. Adding an OpenProcess arm would have to add a variant, which breaks the length assertion and the totality cross-check. Absence is enforced by the count, not by a comment.

EXACT windows-sys 0.61.2 DECLARATIONS, read from the registry source:
  WaitForSingleObject(hhandle, dwmilliseconds: u32) -> WAIT_EVENT   <-- NOT a BOOL
  GetExitCodeProcess(hprocess, lpexitcode: *mut u32) -> BOOL
  TerminateProcess(hprocess, uexitcode: u32) -> BOOL
  QueryFullProcessImageNameW(hprocess, dwflags: PROCESS_NAME_FORMAT, lpexename: PWSTR, lpdwsize: *mut u32) -> BOOL
CONSTANTS: WAIT_OBJECT_0=0, WAIT_ABANDONED=128, WAIT_TIMEOUT=258, WAIT_FAILED=4294967295, INFINITE=4294967295, PROCESS_NAME_WIN32=0, STILL_ACTIVE=0x103=259.

THE TRAP THAT SHAPES THE WHOLE DESIGN. GetExitCodeProcess returns STILL_ACTIVE (259) for a process that is STILL RUNNING, and also returns 259 for a process that genuinely exited with code 259. The two are indistinguishable from the call alone. So an exit code is authoritative ONLY after a wait that returned WAIT_OBJECT_0. Reporting 259 as an exit code without that prior wait is exactly the defect epic rail 4 forbids: unverifiable evidence gaining authority. Model the result as an enum where the exited-with-code case is unconstructible without a confirmed wait.

SECOND NON-COLLAPSE. WaitForSingleObject has FOUR outcomes and only one is an error: WAIT_OBJECT_0 = signalled; WAIT_TIMEOUT = still running, a legitimate Ok value and NOT a failure; WAIT_ABANDONED = 128; WAIT_FAILED = call failed, read GetLastError. A `!= WAIT_OBJECT_0 -> Err` shape is wrong and would make the suspended-process acceptance test unwritable.

CHILD 1 / 2A CONVENTIONS TO FOLLOW: NativeError code 0 means "our refusal, not the OS's" (job.rs:78, and 2a's prove_membership/resume). RawHandle has no Debug so a future derive fails to compile. ProcessSpec and CreatedProcess are deliberately not Debug for the same reason.
